minutes.headline: Planning Board continued the AT&T water tower antenna hearing to March 26 pending an RF exposure statement.
minutes.summary: The board heard an AT&T subcontractor's special permit application to add three antennas to the water district tower, along with an abutter's letter raising RF safety, GPS access, light and noise complaints. Members approved the waiver requests, asked for an RF compliance statement and a timer on the light, and continued the hearing. The board also took committee reports, voted to strike the ten acre requirement from an overlay bylaw, and authorized the chair to sign decisions for this year.

public_comment.topic: Abutter's letter read into the record (via a board member) raising RF safety from added antennas, GPS sending vendors up her driveway, lights left on at night, and loud equipment noise.

votes.motion: Approve all waivers requested by the applicant.
Continue the AT&T special permit hearing to March 26.
Strike the ten acre requirement from the overlay district bylaw.
Allow the chair, for this year's organization of the board, to sign decisions on behalf of the board.

budget_items.what_was_said: The task force reported an application including the recommended projects and fees to offset some town employee costs.

decisions.decision: Board will send the water department a friendly reminder about nighttime lighting and likely condition a timer on the light.
Applicant to submit an engineer's RF compliance statement by Thursday, with the hearing continued to March 26.
Board will request feedback from the Board of Selectmen on a case-by-case basis.
Director to draft a survey on solar and adult-use marijuana and bring the topics to future agendas.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the AT&T special permit hearing for three added water tower antennas to March 26, pending an engineer's RF compliance statement.
The board approved all waivers the applicant requested; the minutes record the vote outcome as not audible.
The board plans to remind the water department about nighttime lighting and is likely to condition a timer on the light.
The board voted to strike the ten acre requirement from the overlay district bylaw.
The board voted to let the chair sign decisions on its behalf for this year's organization of the board.

why_it_matters: The tower sits on water district land, and the abutter's RF, light and noise concerns will be answered in the permit conditions, so the March 26 hearing is where neighbors can see them settled.
Striking the ten acre requirement from the overlay district bylaw changes what parcels the overlay can cover, a change that may later come before voters as a zoning amendment.
watch_next: March 26 continued hearing on the AT&T special permit, and the engineer's RF compliance statement due Thursday.
A director-drafted survey on solar and adult-use marijuana, and those topics on future agendas.
